book.title: Yes! 50 Scientifically Proven Ways to Be Persuasive
book.author: Noah J. Goldstein, Steve J. Martin and Robert B. Cialdini

confidence_note: Figures are from the published study (PMC article) that chapter 2 of the book draws on; the book's own wording was not read, so only the study's figures are used and the 33 percent is computed. Old text's Arizona setting, '33 percent increase' and message wordings were dropped. Replications are mixed and mentioned.
facts: Chapter 2 asks what shifts the bandwagon effect into another gear; the work is by Goldstein, Cialdini and Griskevicius.

Study 1: standard environmental message (help save the environment) 35.1 percent towel reuse; message saying almost 75 percent of guests reuse towels 44.1 percent; 80 days of data, first eligible day per guest, stays of at least two nights.
Study 2: same-room message 49.3 percent, other norm messages combined 42.8 percent, standard message 37.2 percent; all norm messages cited about 75 percent from an earlier study.
49.3 against 37.2 is about a third more reuse (computed).
Some replications found the general norm but not the same-room norm raised reuse.
scene_details: A message in a hotel bathroom asking guests to reuse towels.
The words 'guests who stayed in this room'.
About 75 percent, the same figure in every norm message.
tension: Same towels, same figure, but the group named in the message changed the result.
opening_idea: Start with the standard hotel request and its reuse rate.

lessons.idea: Name the people most like your listener when you say what others do.
lessons.anchor: Same-room message beat the general guest message.

reflect_final: When you tell someone what most people do, which group could you name that is closest to their own situation?

use_cases.situation: Asking a team to use a new tool
use_cases.move: Guests in the same room reused more towels; I'll say what the team down the corridor already does.
Tell them what people in your own building already do.

use_cases.situation: Encouraging a friend to a routine
use_cases.move: Say what people in their own situation do.

pocket_idea: The guests who shared a room beat guests in general.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Same message, one extra phrase: the room.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Study 2 numbers and the closest group effect.
